FINAL SUBMISSION

What I changed: one tensor — `model.language_model.layers.23.self_attn.o_proj.weight` — I zeroed the output block of attention head 6 in layer 23 (columns 1536:1792 of shape [1024, 2048]). No other tensors are edited; the final norm, embeddings/lm_head, and vision tower are untouched. The edit is in `/work/edited` (backed up at `/work/best_head6`).

Evidence:
- Diagnosis: the original weights were 6.6% accurate on baseline practice generations; 95.1% of answers hit the 8192-token cap and never emitted `</think>`, trapped in "Wait …" self-correction repetition loops; the 25 that finished were 100% correct.
- Teacher-forced attribution on those loop texts: the direct logit effect on the "Wait" token at loop positions is dominated by layer-23 full attention (~+162 of ~+172 total; other layers ≤ 3.4; MLP ~+3, top units 66/16/43/346/41). Empirical check also showed final logits behave like E[T]·(h/rms(h)) (stored final-norm weight is not effectively applied).
- Causal tests (paired n=1 on the 256 "select" problems, same seeds, vs cached original 6.25%): heads 0–3 ablated −0.78pp; heads 4–7 ablated +3.91pp; heads 6–7 +3.52pp; head 6 alone +4.69pp (21 wrong→right, 9 right→wrong, 10.94%); 5 MLP units +1.95pp; head6+units +3.12pp (worse); global Arditi removal of the loop direction −3.91pp (harmful, rejected). Head 6 alone was the best simple candidate, so it was kept.
- Confirmation on "confirm_1" (not used for any choice): +0.78pp (12 vs 13 of... actually 34 vs 32 correct, 14 wrong→right vs 12 right→wrong), i.e. no significant gain; accuracy non-decrease. "confirm_2" was not reached because the time limit arrived, so I did not run it.

Strength of evidence — honest assessment: mechanism is coherent and directionally consistent (specificity: heads 0–3 ≈ 0, head 6 positive twice, global-direction removal harmful). But statistical power is limited (SE ≈ 2pp per 256-generation split): select gave +4.7pp, confirm_1 gave +0.8pp. The expected unseen-test gain is therefore likely small positive (roughly 0 to +5pp, point estimate ≈ +2–3pp), with low risk of harm (both 256-answer confirmations were ≥ 0). I chose this over reverting to the original (score 0) because both independent measurements were non-negative and the mechanistic attribution implicates exactly this component.

Why it should help: layer-23 head 6 acts as a repetition/induction writer that injects enormous logit mass toward continuing the "Wait …" re-check loop at exactly those positions; deleting its write into the residual stream weakens the loop attractor, letting the model more often finish its thinking and emit a graded \boxed answer instead of being cut off. Known limitation: the effect size on unseen problems is uncertain; the model's underlying math capability (not the loop) then becomes the bottleneck.
